\begin{example} \end{example}[two-neighborhood criterion]

1. ch0:4.5

If $M$ can be covered by two coordinate neighborhoods $V_1,V_2$ with $V_1\cap V_2$ connected, then $M$ is orientable: the determinant of the change of coordinates has constant sign on the connected $V_1\cap V_2$, and if negative one changes the sign of one coordinate to make it positive throughout. \end{example}
